search_log: Searched "Absolute Power" "David Baldacci" excerpt, first chapter, and ISBN variants; opened the AbeBooks permission-reprinted Chapter One and checked Google Books/Open Library previews.
Searched "Absolute Power" David Baldacci third person, point of view, narrator, and omniscient; opened SoBrief and The StoryGraph's explicit POV descriptions.

Searched publisher and author domains, including Hachette/Grand Central, Pan Macmillan, and davidbaldacci.com; publisher/author pages verified the work but did not provide diagnostic narrator evidence, while direct Hachette sample URLs were inaccessible.
Searched for epistolary, diary, frame narrative, multiple narrators, alternating narration, and epilogue evidence; found no credible indication of sustained first- or second-person base sections.
Opened additional online prose pages and an Open Library record during discovery; unauthorized or catalog-only material was not relied upon as strong evidence.
person_note: The diagnostic quotes show a nonparticipating narrator moving through third-person scenes centered on Jack, Kate, Dan, and other characters; dialogue and generic 'you' statements are local or gnomic, not second-person narration. The authorized opening independently uses sustained third person, and the whole-book web description identifies omniscient narration with shifting character focus rather than changes of grammatical person. No first-person base section or frame was found. Confidence is medium because the Tier A source covers only the opening and the whole-book structural sources are weaker.
